question.leadin: A powerful family that ruled this city included men like Lorezno the Magnificent.
question.text: Name this Italian city once ruled by the Medici family. This city is the most populous one in Tuscany.
question.clue: After Turin and before Rome became capital, it was the capital of the Kingdom of Italy.

swap.leadin: The Strait of Messina separates it from Italy.
swap.text: The Salso river flows through which island with capital Palermo?
swap.clue: A civil war in this place ended via the Treaty of Caltabellota, while Muslim rule of this place ended with the invasion of a man who would fight Alexius Comnenus at Dyrrhachium and had Bohemund as his son.

question.leadin: This leader is known as the "Hero of Two Worlds" for his leadership in the Ragamuffin War and the Uruguayan Civil War. --.
question.text: Name this leader of the Redshirts, who fought the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies during the Expedition of the Thousand in the Risorgimento.
question.clue: He was ordered not to attack Trentino, but he earlier defeated the Neapolitans at the Volturno River.

swap.text: This prime minister of the Kingdom of Piedmont-Sardinia and founder of the newspaper Il Risorgimento became the first prime minister of the unified Kingdom of Italy.
swap.clue: This politician ceded Nice and Savoy to that other leader in exchange for assistance in a war that included the Battle of Solferino.

question.text: This grand duchy north of Rome was briefly replaced by the Kingdom of Etruria, then ruled by Napoleon's sister Elisa. It later federated with Parma and Modena as a client state of Sardinia-Piedmont.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the island of Malta.
swap.text: A Maltese fort named for this patron saint of sailors defended the island against an Ottoman invasion in 1565. This saint's namesake "fire" is a nautical weather phenomenon involving plasma being generated in an electric field.

question.text: The most infamous incident in the Years of Lead was the kidnapping and assassination of this Prime Minister of Italy by the Red Brigades terrorist group.
question.clue: The trial at Turin of Renato Curcio and fourteen other accused terrorists placed him in danger.

swap.leadin: He went through a war with the Duke of Calambria.
swap.text: Name this member of a prominent Italian banking family who ruled during a certain city's Golden Age. He is nicknamed "the Magnificent."
swap.clue: His father, nicknamed the "Gouty," and his son, nicknamed the "Unfortunate," were both named Piero.

question.leadin: Three divisions of this group, nicknamed "Black Flames," "Black Feathers," and "God Wills It," were sent to fight for the Nationalists in the Spanish Civil War.
question.text: Name this volunteer paramilitary group, disbanded in 1943, which was divided into maniples, cohorts, and legions, just like the Roman army.
question.answerHtml: Blackshirts [or Milizia Volontaria per la Sicurezza Nazionale; or MVSN; or camicie nere; or CCNN; or squadristi]
question.clue: Many members of this group made up the M battalions.

swap.leadin: This body's officials served a term of two months before being replaced by officials from other families.
swap.text: Identify this legislative body, which included such positions as the Gonfaloniere of Justice, and expanded in size after the fall of the Albizzi.

question.leadin: "Sweet the memory is to me, of a land beyond the sea." Name some things about Amalfi, for 3, plus 3, plus 4 points each.
question.text: The Italian Duchy of Amalfi was a longtime Mediterranean economic dynamo, prior to its being eclipsed by this other "Most Serene Republic," which was brought to possess great wealth by doges such as Enrico Dandolo.
question.answerHtml: Republic of Venice [accept Venetian Republic; prompt on “La Serenissima”]
question.clue: Enrico Dandolo of this polity successfully diverted the 4th Crusade to sack Constantinople, and ships supplied by this polity won a decisive victory at the Battle of Lepanto.

swap.text: This Florentine writer wrote the treatise De Monarchia to oppose Boniface VIII's declaration of Papal Supremacy in the bull Unam Sanctam. This poet marked Boniface as destined for hell in his best known work.
swap.clue: In one of his works, the letter P is erased from his forehead each time he passes a terrace.

question.text: The exclusion of non-guild members from civic government led to this 14th-century uprising of textile workers in Florence. The wool carder Michele di Lando and the so-called "Eight Saints" led this three-year revolt.
question.clue: Precipitated by the dominance of the Albizi family and the lack of a response from the Signoria, those who took part in this event were led by such men as Luigi di Guiccciardini and Michele di Lando.

swap.text: The Battle of Legnano took place during the war between the Ghibellines and this rival faction, who had supported the papacy and included such members as Henry the Proud and Henry the Lion.
swap.clue: Charles of Anjou helped this group in establishing themselves in their most important city where the Donati and Cerchi families created "black" and "white" factions, Florence.

question.text: This capital of the Ambrosian Republic was ruled by the Visconti beforehand and afterwards by the family of the man who betrayed it, Francesco I Sforza. This northern Italian city is the capital of Lombardy.
question.clue: This city's last independent ruler was Ludovico il Moro, and Gian Galeazzo and Filippo Maria were members of this city's Visconti family.

swap.text: Francis retook Milan by defeating some Swiss cantons and Maximilian Sforza at the 1515 Battle of Marignano, thus ending this phase of the Italian Wars.
swap.answer: War of the League of Cambrai
swap.clue: The defeat of an army of Swiss pikemen by a superior Franco-Venetian force at the Battle of Marignano helped spur the end of this war.

question.leadin: A former writer for a magazine whose name translates as "the manifesto" analogized this organization's trajectory to that of the legendary Tailor of Ulm in a 2009 book that was republished by Verso in 2011.
question.text: Name this organization, whose leaders advocated a theory known as "polycentrism." One of this organization's founders, Palmiro Togliatti ("toll-YAH-tee"), names a city that was the headquarters of VAZ.
question.answerHtml: Italian Communist Party [or PCI; or Partito Comunista Italiano; prompt on Communist Party or Partito Comunista] (The magazine is titled Il Manifesto. The city is Tolyatti, Russia.)
question.clue: This organization joined the CLN on the eve of World War II as part of a strategy known as the Salerno turn.

swap.text: After retiring, Cassiodorus founded this monastery on his property in Squillace ("squee-LAH-chay") near the Castellum. While at this monastery, whose name means "fishpond," Cassiodorus wrote the encyclopedic handbook Institutes.

question.text: The Beinecke also keeps many of these late medieval maps, which used known distances between coastal cities and straight "rhumb lines" along compass directions to draw the Mediterranean and other sea outlines extremely accurately.
question.answerHtml: portolan charts [or portulan maps; prompt on compass chart; prompt on rhumb chart]
question.clue: Contrasting with the large-scale T-O maps of the three continents are these medieval maps of coastlines which are constructed using a network of rhumblines radiating from compasses spread around the map.

swap.text: Zeno eventually came to see Odoacer as a major rival, causing him to offer Italy to this Ostrogothic ruler, who killed Odoacer during a banquet.
swap.clue: He won the original Battle of the Isonzo, which led to an amusing banquet in which he toasted - and then personally strangled - the man who had deposed Romulus Augustulus.
